limitations: Change detection compares exact values. A swap with small edits on top is caught by a near-match pass and reported as a probable swap with medium confidence; other edits to a swapped or copied profile show as value edits.
The tool shows what changed, not which release is correct. Every repair needs a person's decision.

plain_summary: Blocked: A1 can't be trusted on this release yet, because measurements are attached to the wrong samples. First step: restore 2 sample profile(s) in protein_rppa.tsv.gz from the baseline release. Compared with frozen-A, release practice-B has 1 sample swap(s), 5 profile(s) copied onto other IDs, 1 membership change(s). The losses are concentrated in one group: Her2 lost 5 of 61 genuine profiles (8.2%), against 0.8% or less for every other PAM50Call_RNAseq group, so results for Her2 move more than the total count suggests. Random losses would be this concentrated with probability 8.2e-05 (hypergeometric test); that fits a targeted removal or a filtering error, and the tool can't tell which. The 12 changed samples come from 7 tissue source sites, with no sign that one site drives the changes. Sample count unchanged (747) but membership changed: 5 sample(s) removed and 5 added. A count check alone would miss this. A1 is Blocked because of F1, F2, F3, F4; A2 is unaffected and was not rerun. A1 moved 0.37× its sampling noise (within sampling noise); the proposed repairs bring it back to baseline. Small shifts don't make a release safe: verdicts come from what changed, not how much. A person must review before the new release is used.
